# sysutils_alternatives (Resource)

Selects the alternative a link group of the alternatives system points to, such as which program `/usr/bin/editor` or `java` runs, with `update-alternatives` on Debian, Ubuntu and SUSE or `alternatives` on Fedora and RHEL (detected automatically). The selection is made in manual mode, so that installing a package with a higher-priority alternative does not change it. With `link` and `priority`, an alternative that no package registered is registered first (`--install`). The link group is read with `update-alternatives --query` or `alternatives --display`, so a different selection, a return to automatic mode or a removed alternative shows up as drift. On destroy the link group returns to automatic mode or, with `remove_on_destroy`, the alternative is unregistered. Commands are serialised with package manager commands of the provider, which run the same tools from package scripts. Requires root privileges.

It covers the same ground as Ansible's `community.general.alternatives` module.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Make vim the system editor. The alternative is registered by the vim
# package; the selection is pinned in manual mode.
resource "sysutils_alternatives" "editor" {
  name = "editor"
  path = "/usr/bin/vim.basic"
}

# Register a JDK unpacked outside the package manager as an alternative of
# java, select it, and unregister it again on destroy.
resource "sysutils_alternatives" "java" {
  name              = "java"
  path              = "/opt/jdk-21/bin/java"
  link              = "/usr/bin/java"
  priority          = 2100
  remove_on_destroy = true
}

output "editor_mode" {
  value = sysutils_alternatives.editor.mode
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the link group, such as `"editor"` or `"java"`. ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `+`, `@`, `:`, `~` and `-`, starting with a letter, digit or `_`. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `path` (String) The alternative to select, such as `"/usr/bin/vim.basic"`: an absolute, canonical path without white space. It must be registered in the link group already, unless `link` and `priority` are set to register it.

### Optional

- `link` (String) The link group's master link, such as `"/usr/bin/editor"`. With `priority`, `path` is registered with `--install <link> <name> <path> <priority>` whenever it is not registered, or the group's link or the alternative's priority differ; these then count as drift. An existing group's link is renamed to it. Requires `priority`.
- `priority` (Number) Priority `path` is registered with, used to pick an alternative in automatic mode; the highest wins. A 32-bit signed integer. Requires `link`.
- `remove_on_destroy` (Boolean) What happens on destroy. If `false`, the link group returns to automatic mode (`--auto`), and `path` stays registered. If `true`, `path` is unregistered (`--remove`), which selects the best remaining alternative, or removes the link group and its links if it was the last one. Use `true` for alternatives registered through `link` and `priority`. Defaults to `false`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Resource identifier (equal to `name`).
- `mode` (String) Mode of the link group: `manual` once the resource selected `path`, `auto` if the group was returned to automatic mode outside Terraform. The resource always plans `manual`, so a return to automatic mode is drift that the next apply reverts.

## Behavior

The provider uses `update-alternatives` from dpkg if it is in `PATH` and is not a symlink to `alternatives`, as it is on Fedora and RHEL; otherwise `alternatives` from chkconfig. Hosts with neither, such as Alpine, fail with an error. Every command runs with an argument vector, never through a shell, in the C locale and with a limit of 2 minutes.

### Create and Update

1. The link group is read with `update-alternatives --query <name>` or `alternatives --display <name>`.
2. If `link` and `priority` are set, `path` is registered with `--install <link> <name> <path> <priority>` if it is not registered yet, or if the group's master link or the alternative's priority differ. This creates the link group if it does not exist, and renames its master link if it has another one.
3. Without `link` and `priority`, `path` must already be registered, for example by the package that installed it. Otherwise the apply fails with an error that lists the registered alternatives.
4. Unless the group is already in manual mode and points to `path`, it is switched with `--set <name> <path>`. The provider then reads the group again and fails if it does not point to `path` in manual mode.

Manual mode keeps the selection when a package later registers an alternative with a higher priority, which would take over in automatic mode.

Changing `name` replaces the resource. Changing `path` selects the new alternative; the previous one stays registered.

### Destroy

- With `remove_on_destroy = false`, the default, the link group returns to automatic mode with `--auto <name>`, which selects the alternative with the highest priority. `path` stays registered. Nothing happens if the group is in automatic mode already or no longer exists.
- With `remove_on_destroy = true`, `path` is unregistered with `--remove <name> <path>`. If it was selected, the tools select the best remaining alternative in automatic mode; if it was the last one, they remove the link group and its links. Nothing happens if `path` is not registered.

### Locking

The tools rewrite the link group's administrative file (`/var/lib/dpkg/alternatives/<name>` or `/var/lib/alternatives/<name>`) and its symlinks without locking, and package scripts run them during installs. All commands of this resource therefore hold the provider's package-manager lock, which also serialises `sysutils_package` and `sysutils_package_repository`, so that they never overlap with a package install by the provider or with each other. See [Concurrency and Locking](../index.md#concurrency-and-locking).

## Validation

- `name` must be at most 255 characters matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.+@:~-]*$`. It can therefore never be taken for an option of the tools, and never name a file outside their administrative directory.
- `path` and `link` must be absolute and canonical (no `.`, `..`, duplicate or trailing `/`), not `/`, at most 4096 bytes, and free of white space and control characters, which the output of `alternatives --display` and the administrative files cannot represent. A value starting with `-` is never absolute, so it can't be taken for an option either.
- `link` and `priority` must be set together, and `link` must differ from `path`. `priority` must fit a 32-bit signed integer.

## Drift Detection

On refresh the provider reads the link group:

- If the group does not exist, the resource is removed from the state, and the next apply creates it again, which needs `link` and `priority`.
- `path` is set to the alternative the group points to. If it was switched to another alternative, the plan shows `path` changing back. If the group points to an alternative that is no longer registered, or to none, `path` is empty.
- `mode` is `auto` if the group was returned to automatic mode; since the resource always plans `manual`, the next apply sets it again.
- If `link` is set, it is refreshed from the group's master link; if `priority` is set, from the priority `path` is registered with. A change of either shows up as drift and the next apply registers `path` again. `alternatives --display` does not show the master link, so on Fedora and RHEL it is read from the second line of `/var/lib/alternatives/<name>`.

## Import

A link group can be imported by name:

```shell
# By the name of the link group. The alternative it points to becomes path;
# link and priority are left unset.
terraform import sysutils_alternatives.editor editor
```

`path` is the alternative the group points to, and `remove_on_destroy` is `false`. `link` and `priority` are left unset; if the configuration sets them, the first apply registers `path` with them. The import fails if the link group does not exist.

## Caveats

- The resource requires root, as the tools do.
- Only the master link is managed. Follower (slave) links, such as manual pages, are those the alternative was registered with; `--install` from this resource registers none, and replaces those of an existing registration of `path`.
- The resource cannot be used with the provider's `root_dir` argument: the tools always change the running host, so it refuses to plan when `root_dir` is set.
- Destroying a resource whose `path` was installed by a package, with `remove_on_destroy = true`, unregisters the package's alternative until the package is reinstalled. Keep the default for alternatives that packages manage.
